c1.label: Q1
c1.prompt: The two rainbow lights under the car come from which extension?

A.text: They are built into the micro:bit

c1.why: They sit on pin P15 and belong to the neopixel extension. That is why this chapter needs two extensions, not one.

c2.label: Q2
c2.prompt: In an LED strip of two lights, what number is the first one?
c2.why: Strips count from 0. With two lights they are 0 and 1 — there is no light number 2.

c3.label: Q3
c3.prompt: `repeat 5 times` versus `forever` — what is the difference?

C.text: There is no difference for lights

c3.why: An indicator blinks a set number of times and stops. That is exactly what `repeat` is for.

r1.label: Q1
r1.why: Light 0 is the first of the two. `show` is what actually sends the color out to the strip.

r2.label: Q2

D.text: Nothing — the color was never sent out

r2.why: `set pixel color` writes the color into memory. Until `show` runs, the strip has not been told anything.

r3.label: Q3
r3.prompt: How long does this take from start to finish?

A.text: About two and a half seconds

r3.why: Each trip is on for half a second and off for half a second — one second. Five trips make five seconds.

r4.label: Q4
r4.prompt: You press A and then leave the car alone. What happens after the five blinks?

A.text: The lamp stays off until you press again

r4.why: The repeat finishes, the last block left the lamp off, and the handler goes back to waiting for the next press.

d1.label: Q1
d1.prompt: The lamp never appears to light up at all. What is missing?
d1.why: On and off arrive within a fraction of a millisecond. The gap is the blink — without it there is nothing for an eye to catch.

d2.label: Q2
d2.prompt: A pair set the strip up inside the button block. Why is that a problem?

A.text: Pin P15 only works in `on start`

C.text: The strip cannot be used with buttons

D.text: It is rebuilt on every press instead of once at the start

d2.why: Setting up is a once-at-the-beginning job. Doing it again on every press is how the lights end up confused.

b1.label: Q1
b1.prompt: Put these in order for one blink of the under-car light: 1 pause · 2 set the pixel color · 3 show · 4 set the color back to black and show it
b1.why: Choose the color, send it out, hold it long enough to see, then clear it. `show` has to come after the color, not before.

b2.label: Q2
b2.prompt: Where does `set up the strip on P15` belong?

A.text: At the very bottom of the program

D.text: In `on start`, before anything uses the strip

b2.why: It has to run once, before any block refers to the strip. That is what "set up" means.
